newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse Electric debt tightens on news.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse Electric debt tightens on news.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp debt tightened 10 to 15 basis points in Wednesday trading after the company announced it would split into two, spinning off its industrial business to focus on its broadcast assets, traders said.
"Westinghouse paper tightened after the news...spreads were between 10 and 15 basis points tighter," one trader said.

The company's 8.625 percent paper due 2012 was seen trading at a tighter spread at 188 basis points bid while the firm's 7.875 percent paper due 2023 tightened to a bid of 195 basis points, traders said.
News that the broadcast company would retain over $2.0 billion in public debt on its balance sheet was met with very good reception by bondholders, traders said.
"The market was anticipating the spin-off, but the question was who the debt would end up with," said one trader.

Meanwhile, investor sentiment on the bonds was boosted when credit rating agency, Standard & Poor's said it was revising the outlook on the firm and units' double-B corporate credit rating to "positive" from "developing."
"On the whole the market has given its vote of confidence to the idea of lumping the debt with the broadcasting assets which have great cash flow," the trader added.
However, S&P said, the outlook on Infinity Broadcasting Corp's BB-plus corporate credit and BB-minus subordinated debt were kept under review with "developing" implications.
Later in the day, Moody's Investors Service announced it affirmed Westinghouse's Ba1 senior unsecured debt.
In addition, Moody's said it affirmed CBS Inc's Ba1 senior unsecured debt and Infinity Broadcasting Corp's Ba3 senior subordinated debt ratings.

Westinghouse Electric said earlier the newly created industrial company will be called Westinghouse Electric Co (WELCO) and will be based in Pittsburgh while the media company will be based in New York, the company said.
